minutes.headline: Select Board opened the 2021 town meeting warrant and adopted a CDL drug and alcohol clearinghouse policy.
minutes.summary: The board opened the annual town meeting warrant, named a liaison for the old primary school landscape design, adopted a federally required clearinghouse policy and authorized a parking easement for the historical society. It discussed hunting and firearms possession on conservation land and deferred the possession question until town counsel gives a formal opinion. The town manager reported on the Flat Hill Road bridge lane closure, a cemetery ADA grant, and department updates.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted 5-0 to approve a federally required drug and alcohol clearinghouse policy for commercial drivers.
The board voted 5-0 to open the annual town meeting warrant on January 12, 2021 and close it March 15, 2021 at 4 p.m.
The board deferred the question of firearms possession on town conservation land until town counsel gives a written opinion and attends a meeting.
The board voted 5-0 to authorize the chair to sign an exclusive parking easement for the historical society.
The town manager said the solid waste contract expires June 30 and costs are expected to rise sharply; the board had no objection to an RFP for the Brooks House building.

why_it_matters: The warrant is how articles reach Town Meeting, so anything a resident wants voted on in spring must be filed before it closes.
The solid waste contract renewal is a likely cost increase that would fall on the town budget, mostly taxes, or on household trash fees, depending on how it is paid.
The firearms question on conservation land stays unsettled until counsel's opinion is delivered at a public meeting.
watch_next: The warrant closes March 15, 2021 at 4 p.m.
Town counsel's written opinion on firearms possession and a meeting appearance, no date given.
